name: integers
description: Boundary integers across every argument width in CBOR's 64-bit range.
note: Values use the fixture description grammar documented in docs/protocol/README.md: {"int": decimal string}, {"bytes": hex}, {"text": string}, {"bool": bool}, {"null": true}, {"array": [value]}, {"map": [[key, value]]}. Map entries are listed in source order; a conforming encoder sorts them into canonical key order.

cases.description: Zero uses a single head byte.
Small unsigned values are encoded in the head.
23 is the largest value carried in the head byte.
24 is the smallest value needing a one-byte argument.
255 is the largest one-byte argument.
256 is the smallest two-byte argument.
65535 is the largest two-byte argument.
65536 is the smallest four-byte argument.
2^32-1 is the largest four-byte argument.
2^32 is the smallest eight-byte argument.
2^64-1 is the largest permitted unsigned value.
-1 is the largest negative value.
-24 is the last negative value carried in the head byte.
-25 is the first negative value needing a one-byte argument.
-256 is the largest one-byte negative argument.
-257 is the smallest two-byte negative argument.
-65536 is the largest two-byte negative argument.
-65537 is the smallest four-byte negative argument.
-2^32 is the largest four-byte negative argument.
-2^32-1 is the smallest eight-byte negative argument.
-2^64 is the smallest permitted value in the profile.
Timestamps are integer UTC milliseconds, never tagged dates.
